regime_montecarlo_decision.summary: A three-state hidden Markov model (flat, uptrend, downtrend) reads ADX, candle bodies, range compression, confirmed swing highs and lows and higher-high / higher-low structure and tracks the current regime bar by bar; a Monte Carlo simulation runs the current regime forward; Kronos forecasts the next candles; FinBERT reads the news; gradient-boosted trees weigh all four and decide whether to trade.
regime_montecarlo_decision.implementationNote: Regime model: cycle/regime_hmm.py StructuralRegimeHMM (docs/regime-hmm.md), exactly three states named and ordered flat, uptrend, downtrend, over eight causal features: Wilder ADX 14, the 14-bar mean candle body-to-range ratio, 14-bar over 100-bar mean true range, the close's distance from the last swing high and low confirmed swing_confirmation_bars bars after it formed (shared.zones.structural_pivots) over the move scale, bars since the last pivot, a decayed higher-high / higher-low counter (half-life 48 bars) and the sign of the last two pivots. Diagonal Gaussian emissions over the features standardised on the training span; hmmlearn GaussianHMM Baum-Welch seeded from a heuristic labelling (flat where ADX < adx_threshold, else up / down by the counter's sign), transition diagonal initialised at 0.95 with a sticky Dirichlet prior, a variance floor and a Gaussian prior holding each state's mean near its seed after every iteration, up to regime_fit_iteration_count iterations, states ordered by the counter's mean; the walk uses the forward filter, never the smoother. Monte Carlo: per regime a Student-t of the one-bar log return (scipy maximum likelihood on the training bars the forward filter puts in it); simulation_count paths of the label horizon start from the filtered regime probabilities and re-draw the regime each bar from the transition matrix, with common random numbers. Kronos: the pretrained foundation model (kronos_model_size, pinned Hugging Face revision) reads the last kronos_context_bars candles and decodes the next horizon candles greedily. FinBERT: the nine finbert_* columns. Decision model: xgboost over the three regime probabilities, the simulation's P(up), expected move and 10-90 percentile spread, Kronos' move and direction and the FinBERT columns, the regime and simulation signals of the last maximum_training_bars training rows made out of fold (stacking_fold_count blocks, each purged by the label horizon on both sides), early-stopped on validation. The trade gate is a share gate: gate_open_fraction is the largest share of bars it opens on, most confident first; the fold's absolute threshold is the smallest |P - 0.5| with at most that share of the kept decision model's validation probabilities at or beyond it (its purged out-of-fold training probabilities when a fold has fewer than 50 validation rows), and the gate opens when |P - 0.5| is at or beyond it. Bars with the same probability are admitted together or not at all, so when the model gives one probability to more bars than the share allows the gate stays shut. The price model is the simulation's expected move. Expect: regimes describe trend and range well; direction is close to the base rate.
regime_montecarlo_decision.estimatedTrainingTime: 10-60 min (paced replay; Kronos reads every test bar on the GPU)

adx_threshold.label: ADX flat threshold
adx_threshold.description: Training bars whose average directional index (ADX 14) is below this seed the flat regime before Baum-Welch refines it; at or above it, the higher-high / higher-low score's sign seeds uptrend or downtrend.

swing_confirmation_bars.label: Swing confirmation (bars)
swing_confirmation_bars.description: A swing high is a bar whose high is above the highs of this many bars on each side (the mirror for a swing low), so a pivot is known only this many bars after it forms.

regime_fit_iteration_count.label: Regime fit iterations
regime_fit_iteration_count.description: Most Baum-Welch (expectation-maximisation) iterations of the structural hidden Markov model fit; it stops sooner when the log-likelihood gains less than 0.01.

simulation_count.label: Simulated paths
simulation_count.description: Monte Carlo paths of the label horizon simulated at every bar from the current regime probabilities.

kronos_model_size.label: Kronos model
kronos_model_size.description: Which pretrained Kronos forecasts the next candles: mini (4.1 million parameters, fastest), small (24.7 million) or base (102.3 million).

kronos_context_bars.label: Kronos context (bars)
kronos_context_bars.description: Candles ending at the bar that Kronos reads before it forecasts the next ones.

stacking_fold_count.label: Out-of-fold blocks
stacking_fold_count.description: Contiguous blocks the stacking rows are cut into; each block's regime and simulation signals come from a regime model fitted without it (purged by the label horizon).

maximum_training_bars.label: Stacking rows
maximum_training_bars.description: The most recent training rows the decision model is fitted on (each needs a Kronos forecast and a simulation).

boosting_rounds.label: Decision model boosting rounds
boosting_rounds.description: Most boosting rounds of the decision model (early stopping ends sooner when validation stops improving).

max_depth.label: Decision model tree depth
max_depth.description: Deepest split chain of each decision tree.

gate_open_fraction.label: Largest share of bars the trade gate opens on, most confident first
gate_open_fraction.description: The engine enters a trade only on the bars where the decision model's probability is furthest from 0.5. This is the largest share of bars that may qualify: at fit, the fold's threshold is the smallest distance |P - 0.5| with at most this share of the kept decision model's probabilities on the validation rows at or beyond it (the purged out-of-fold training probabilities when a fold has fewer than 50 validation rows). Bars with the same probability qualify together or not at all, so the gate can open on less than this share, and stays shut when the model gives one probability to more bars than the share allows. 1.0 opens the gate on every bar.

native.produces: A three-state hidden Markov model gives the probability that each bar is in a flat, uptrend or downtrend regime from the average directional index, the candle body-to-range ratio, range compression, the distances from the confirmed swing high and swing low and the higher-high and higher-low structure, a regime-switching Student-t simulation turns those probabilities into a fan of price paths over the label horizon, and gradient-boosted trees weigh that fan with the Kronos candle forecast and the FinBERT news columns into one probability that the close will be higher.
native.targetVariable: The hidden trend regime of each bar (flat, uptrend or downtrend), the distribution of the one-bar log return given that regime, and the probability that the close label horizon bars ahead is above this bar's close.
native.objectiveNote: The regime model is fitted by expectation maximisation (Baum-Welch) on the sequence likelihood of the eight structural features, seeded from a heuristic labelling and held near its seed means by a prior, each regime then gets its own Student-t of the one-bar log return by maximum likelihood on the training bars the forward filter assigns to it, and only the final gradient-boosted trees over the stacked signals are fitted on the direction label.

metrics.why: The forward filter gives a one-step-ahead density for the next bar's structural features (average directional index, body-to-range ratio, range compression, swing distances, bars since the last pivot, higher-high and higher-low score and the sign of the last two pivots), and this is the score of that density on test bars the Baum-Welch fit never saw, so it says whether the flat, uptrend and downtrend emissions learned on the training span still describe the tape; it grades the structural features and not the return.
metrics.baseline: The held-out density of a single diagonal Gaussian over the same structural features fitted on the same training span, which is the same model with no regime structure.

metrics.why: The simulator's whole output at a bar is the cloud of simulated end-of-horizon moves drawn from the regime-switching Student-t returns, and this score compares that cloud with the move that really happened, rewarding a fan that is both centred and no wider than it needs to be.
metrics.baseline: The same score for a fan drawn from the pooled training returns with no regime switching, and the mean absolute actual move, which is the score of forecasting no move.

metrics.why: The decision trees only earn their place if their probability of up scores better than the simulation's own share of paths ending higher, and better than the same trees refitted with the Kronos signals or the FinBERT columns removed, on the same folds.
metrics.baseline: The simulation's own probability of up on the same scored bars, and the same decision trees with one signal group removed.

metrics.why: Ranking each realised horizon move among the simulated paths of its bar shows whether the fan is too narrow or too wide when the filter says flat, uptrend or downtrend, which the per-regime Student-t scales are meant to prevent, so a rank histogram that is not flat within one regime shows that regime's Student-t scale is wrong.

Grouping test bars by the regime the forward filter thinks most likely shows whether the absolute forward move, and the up share, differ from regime to regime, which is the whole reason the simulation starts from the filtered regime probabilities.
metrics.baseline: The up share and the mean absolute forward move of all scored bars of the same series.

metrics.why: The three regimes carry fixed names ordered by the mean of the higher-high and higher-low counter, and the decision trees read each regime probability by that name, so this checks that bars two adjacent folds share receive the same regime from both fits and that a fold does not swap what uptrend means.

The simulator re-draws the regime on every simulated bar from the fitted transition matrix, so a regime whose runs are shorter than the label horizon adds almost nothing to the fan beyond the pooled return distribution.

A regime to which the forward filter assigns too few training bars falls back to the pooled Student-t of all training returns, so the share of bars per regime shows how many of the three regimes carry a return distribution of their own.

The simulation's probability of up is a share of simulation_count paths, and the same random draws are reused at every bar, so this error bar says how much of a small lean away from one half is the path count and not the regime.

The stack only enters on bars where the trees' probability of up is among the most confident share set by gate_open_fraction, and it can open on fewer bars than that share because bars with equal probability are admitted together or not at all, so the share of bars with an open gate says how often this model has an opinion strong enough to act on at all.

notApplicable.name: Silhouette coefficient
notApplicable.why: The regimes are defined by diagonal Gaussian densities over the structural features and by which regime tends to follow which, so a distance-based tightness score would grade a shape the hidden Markov model never promised.

notApplicable.name: Kronos forecast error as a trained quantity
notApplicable.why: Kronos is a pretrained model that this stack only reads, with greedy decoding and pinned weights, so nothing about it is fitted here and its forecast error is an input property, not a result of this model's training.

notApplicable.name: Training objective value by step for the simulator
notApplicable.why: The Monte Carlo stage minimises nothing step by step; its Student-t parameters come from one maximum-likelihood fit per regime, and only the decision trees have a round-by-round loss curve.

asRun.standInNote: No catalog specification describes this stack, so the adapter code is the definition: the as-run numbers measure the gradient-boosted decision trees' probability of up over the regime, simulation, Kronos and FinBERT signals, traded only where the model's own gate is open, and a separate regime simulation supplies the price forecast.
asRun.probabilityNote: The probability of up is the logistic output of the xgboost decision trees, fitted without class weights on the stacked signals and read at the early-stopped round, so it tracks the training up share and is not the simulation's share of paths ending higher, which is only one of the trees' inputs.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per row, one value per boosting round

meaningful.why: The decision trees are fitted by unweighted logistic loss, so on test bars this is the same quantity they minimised, and it says whether the regime, simulation, Kronos and FinBERT signals together state better odds than quoting the fold's training up share on every bar.

This stack carries its own entry rule, the gate that stands aside on bars where the trees' probability of up is not among the most confident share set by gate_open_fraction, so the money earned after costs tests the direction call and the model's choice of when to act together.
The boosted trees give a continuous probability, so this shows whether bars the stack scored higher really went up more often, separately from whether the size of the stated odds is right.
A bounded second opinion on the trees' stated odds that a handful of very confident wrong bars cannot dominate, read against the score of always quoting the fold's training up share.

The gate acts on the distance of the probability from one half, so a slope below one, meaning the trees' leans are larger than the outcomes justify, would mean the gate opens on confidence that is not real.

The trees are fitted without class weights, so their probability is meant to match observed up shares directly, and the binned gap is a fair check, read with the occupied-bin count because the probabilities of this stack sit close to one half.

Per-bar net money over its spread for the gated calls of this stack, with bars on which the closed gate left it flat counted as zero, so a wider gate lowers both the return and the risk it is divided by.
The deepest fall in the money curve of the gated calls, which shows whether standing aside on low-conviction bars actually kept the stack out of its worst stretches.
The gated direction calls of this stack against simply holding the same contract through the same folds, which is the same-series reference for a model whose probability stays near the base rate.

The price forecast is the mean simulated move of the regime-switching Student-t paths, so this tests the regime model and the simulator alone, without the trees, against forecasting no move on the same bars.
Money won over money lost across the closed trades the open gate allowed, which describes how the gated entries pay off and is not a no-skill reference at one because every trade pays costs.
The share of the gated trades that closed with a profit after costs, read together with the trade count because a tight gate can leave only a few trades per fold.

The engine scores the up or down call of every bar at one half whether or not the gate was open, so this is the hit rate of the trees' lean on all scored bars, most of which the stack itself would not have traded.
Because the unweighted trees lean toward the training majority direction, the mean of the up recall and the down recall shows whether the calls do more than repeat that majority.
One symmetric number for the every-bar calls of the trees that stays near zero when the stack calls nearly every bar the same direction, which accuracy alone would hide.

The spread of the trees' probability around its mean decides how many distinct distances from one half exist for the share gate to rank, so a very small spread or few distinct probabilities leaves the gate shut or nearly shut.
A closed gate makes no new entry, so the share of bars with no position is this model's own behaviour and shows how much of the tape it chose to sit out under the holding period in force.
The number of closed trades the gate allowed, which is the sample every trade-level number of this stack rests on and grows with gate_open_fraction.

The price forecast comes from the simulation alone and the traded call from the trees, so the share of bars on which their directions agree shows how far Kronos and FinBERT moved the decision away from the regime simulation.
The average size, in points, of the miss of the simulation's mean move, read beside the no-change forecast error on the same bars because a mean of many simulated paths is close to zero.

The sign of the simulation's mean move comes from the Student-t locations of the regimes the filter favours, and after rounding to the tick many forecasts are exactly zero, so it is read with its denominator.
Each regime's Student-t location is the drift seen on its training bars, so a mean forecast error away from zero shows that training-span drift being carried into the test bars.

Both curves are unweighted logarithmic loss of the same trees, so the gap is a fair overfit check, with the note that training rows carry out-of-fold regime signals while validation rows carry signals from the regime model fitted on the whole training span.

The search tunes the flat-regime average directional index seed, the swing confirmation length, the tree depth, the learning rate and the gate's share of bars on blocks of the training span, so this is the selection score that picked them and is optimistic by construction.

How much of the score that chose the regime seed, swing length, tree settings and above all the gate's share of bars survived on the fold's test walk, which matters here because a share chosen on few gated trades is easy to overfit.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The decision trees are fitted without class weights, so their probability targets the base rate and a score that gives each direction half the weight grades a prior this model never aimed at.
It counts the every-bar call at one half, and an unweighted fit near the base rate calls almost every bar the training majority direction, so it says little about the bars the gate actually traded.

caveats: The engine scores the direction call of every bar, but it enters a trade only where this model's own gate is open, and a closed gate makes no new entry while a held position runs to its holding period, so classification numbers cover all scored bars and trading numbers cover only the gated ones.

The price forecast does not come from the decision trees: the engine builds a second copy of the adapter that refits the regime model and reports the mean simulated move, so price-forecast numbers test the regime simulation and never the Kronos or FinBERT signals.

The gate's threshold is the smallest distance from one half that at most gate_open_fraction of the kept model's validation probabilities reach, so the validation rows both stop the boosting and set the gate; bars with equal probability are admitted together or not at all, and a model that gives few distinct probabilities can leave the gate shut for a whole fold, in which case the trading numbers of that fold are empty.
The reported validation loss is the number that stopped the boosting, so it is optimistic and only the test-bar logarithmic loss is a fair score.

Kronos is a pretrained model loaded at a pinned revision, and the adapter does not check whether its pretraining data overlaps the test bars, so its signal may carry knowledge of the period being walked.

Only the regime and simulation signals of the training rows are made out of fold, in stacking_fold_count blocks purged by the label horizon on both sides; the Kronos and FinBERT signals are used as they are because nothing of theirs is fitted on these bars.
The lake holds news for only a small part of the history, so on most bars the FinBERT columns carry no information and the trees decide from the regime, simulation and Kronos signals.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because their horizons overlap, so any interval around these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.

The same random draws are reused at every bar and every fit, so two runs with the same seed agree exactly and a different seed changes the simulated probability by the Monte Carlo error of simulation_count paths.
For roots other than MNQ the commission and fee figures are the MNQ account figures applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its own close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

The explainer cannot reload this model because its saved arrays hold only closes, while the regime model reads open, high and low and Kronos reads whole candles with volume, so the model is explained by the regime forecasts recorded during its run.
